(a) Extension.—Except as otherwise provided in this section and amendments made by this section and notwithstanding any other provision of law, the authorities provided by each provision of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008 (Public Law 110–246; 122 Stat. 1651) and each amendment made by that Act (and for mandatory programs at such funding levels), as in effect on September 30, 2012, shall continue, and the Secretary of Agriculture shall carry out the authorities, until the later of—
        (1) September 30, 2013; or 
        (2) the date specified in the provision of that Act or amendment made by that Act.  
    (b) Commodity Programs.—
        (1) In general.—The terms and conditions applicable to a covered commodity or loan commodity (as those terms are defined in section 1001 of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008 (7 U.S.C. 8702)) or to peanuts, sugarcane, or sugar beets for the 2012 crop year pursuant to title I of that Act (7 U.S.C. 8702 et seq.) and each amendment made by that title shall be applicable to the 2013 crop year for that covered commodity, loan commodity, peanuts, sugarcane, or sugar beets. 
        (2) Milk.—
            (A) In general.—Notwithstanding subsection (a), the Secretary of Agriculture shall carry out the dairy product price support program under section 1501 of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008 (7 U.S.C. 8771) through December 31, 2013. 
            (B) Milk income loss contract program.—Section 1506 of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008 (7 U.S.C. 8773) is amended by striking “2012” each place it appears in subsections (c)(3), (d)(1), (d)(2), (e)(2)(A), (g), and (h)(1) and inserting “2013”.  
        (3) Suspension of permanent price support authorities.—The provisions of law specified in subsections (a) through (c) of section 1602 of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008 (7 U.S.C. 8782) shall be suspended—
            (A) for the 2013 crop or production year of a covered commodity (as that term is defined in section 1001 of that Act (7 U.S.C. 8702)), peanuts, sugarcane, and sugar, as appropriate; and 
            (B) in the case of milk, through December 31, 2013.   
    (c) Conservation Programs.—
        (1) Conservation reserve.—Section 1231(d) of the Food Security Act of 1985 (16 U.S.C. 3831(d)) is amended in the second sentence by striking “and 2012” and inserting “2012, and 2013”. 
        (2) Voluntary public access.—Section 1240R of the Food Security Act of 1985 (16 U.S.C. 3839bb–5) is amended by striking subsection (f) and inserting the following:“(f) Funding.—“(1) Fiscal years 2009 through 2012.—Of the funds of the Commodity Credit Corporation, the Secretary shall use to carry out this section, to the maximum extent practicable, $50,000,000 for the period of fiscal years 2009 through 2012.“(2) Authorization of appropriations.—There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $10,000,000 for fiscal year 2013.”.  
    (d) Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program.—

            (A) in subparagraph (A), by striking “and” after the semicolon at the end; and

    (g) Horticulture and Organic Agriculture Programs.—

        (4) Organic production and market data initiatives.—Section 7407(d) of the Farm Security and Rural Investment Act of 2002 (7 U.S.C. 5925c(d)) is amended—

    (h) Outreach and Technical Assistance for Socially Disadvantaged Farmers or Ranchers.—Section 2501(a)(4) of the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990 (7 U.S.C. 2279(a)(4)) is amended—

        (3) by inserting after subparagraph (A) the following:“(B) Fiscal year 2013.—There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $20,000,000 for fiscal year 2013.”;

    (i) Exceptions.—
        (1) In general.—Subsection (a) does not apply with respect to mandatory funding provided by programs authorized by provisions of law amended by subsections (d) through (h). 
        (2) Conservation.—Subsection (a) does not apply with respect to the programs specified in paragraphs (3)(B), (4), (6), and (7) of section 1241(a) of the Food Security Act of 1985 (16 U.S.C. 3841(a)), relating to the conservation stewardship program, farmland protection program, environmental quality incentives program, and wildlife habitat incentives program, for which program authority was extended through fiscal year 2014 by section 716 of Public Law 112–55 (125 Stat. 582).

        (4) Survey of foods purchased by school food authorities.—Subsection (a) does not apply with respect to section 4307 of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008 (Public Law 110–246; 122 Stat. 1893) relating to the use of Commodity Credit Corporation funds for a survey and report regarding foods purchased by school food authorities.

        (6) Market loss assistance for asparagus producers.—Subsection (a) does not apply with respect to section 10404(d) of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008 (Public Law 110–246; 122 Stat. 2112).

    (j) Effective Date.—Except as otherwise provided in this section, this section and the amendments made by this section take effect on the earlier of—

fable.w: This section only extends existing farm bill authorities for a year, changes dates and funding amounts, and lists exceptions. The tempting reading is that phrases like "Voluntary public access" or the blanket extension of 2008 Act authorities (some of which may involve rulemaking or advisory bodies elsewhere) amount to participation. But those are program names and incorporations by reference; nothing in this section itself requires or authorizes comment periods, hearings, advisory committees, consultation with outside parties, or a right to sue.

qwen_block.w: This section extends the authority of existing agricultural programs and sets funding levels for fiscal year 2013. It does not require the Secretary of Agriculture or any other federal official to consult with, coordinate with, or receive input from non-federal entities (such as states, tribes, farmers, or the public) before making the decision to extend these authorities. The extension is automatic by statute. While the programs themselves may involve interactions with farmers (e.g., applying for loans or grants), the act of extending the program authority does not constitute participation, and applications for benefits are explicitly excluded from the definition.
qwen_block.s: the authorities provided by each provision of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008 ... shall continue, and the Secretary of Agriculture shall carry out the authorities, until the later of— (1) September 30, 2013; or (2) the date specified in the provision of that Act or amendment made by that Act.
qwen_block.b:
To determine the label, I must analyze whether the section involves the federal government consulting or coordinating with people *outside* the government before making a decision.

1.  **Analyze the Text**: The section is titled "Extension" and primarily consists of extending the authorities and funding levels of various agricultural programs (Commodity Programs, Conservation Programs, SNAP, Research Programs, Energy Programs, etc.) from the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008 for the fiscal year 2013.
2.  **Identify Actors**: The primary actor mentioned is the "Secretary of Agriculture" (a federal official). The text mentions "manufacturers," "producers," "farmers," and "ranchers" only in the context of existing program definitions or funding allocations (e.g., "covered commodity," "loan commodity," "beginning farmer").
3.  **Check for Participation Mechanisms**:
    *   **Consultation/Coordination**: Does the Secretary consult with states, tribes, or the public *before* extending these authorities? No. The extension is automatic by statute ("shall continue").
    *   **Advisory Boards**: Are there any new advisory boards created or referenced that include non-federal members? No.
    *   **Public Comment/Hearings**: Is there a requirement for a comment period or hearing? No.
    *   **Right to Sue**: Is there a grant of right to sue? No.
    *   **Applications**: The text mentions "pending rural development loan and grant applications" in subsection (i)(5)(B), but this is an exception to the extension, not a participation mechanism. Applying for a grant is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.
4.  **Evaluate "Tempting" Readings**: One might look at "Outreach and Technical Assistance for Socially Disadvantaged Farmers" (subsection h) and think this involves interaction with the public. However, the text only authorizes funding for this program; it does not describe a process where the government *consults* with these farmers to make a decision. It is an administrative extension of funding. Similarly, "Conservation Programs" involve farmers, but the text only extends the authority to run the programs, not a specific participatory decision-making process for this extension.
5.  **Conclusion**: The section is a legislative extension of existing authorities and funding. It does not impose a new requirement for the federal government to consult with outside parties before making the decision to extend these programs. The decision is made by Congress via this statute. Therefore, there is no participation as defined.

opus.w: This section extends existing farm bill authorities and funding levels through 2013, mostly by changing dates and authorizing money. It creates no comment period, hearing, rulemaking authority, outside advisory body, required consultation with outsiders, or right to sue. Names like "Voluntary public access," "Outreach and Technical Assistance," and "Pigford claims" might look like participation, but they are just program titles or references to funding and benefit claims. The general extension of the 2008 Act's authorities does not itself spell out any outside-party process.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an extension of existing authorities and funding levels for various agricultural programs. It does not itself establish any new requirement for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties (such as states, tribes, or the public) before making a decision. It merely continues the status quo of previous laws. While the underlying programs might involve participation, this specific statutory text is a funding/authority extension and does not contain the procedural language defining participation (e.g., public comment, advisory boards, consultation).
qwen_chat.s: (a) Extension.—Except as otherwise provided in this section and amendments made by this section and notwithstanding any other provision of law, the authorities provided by each provision of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008 (Public Law 110–246; 122 Stat. 1651) and each amendment made by that Act (and for mandatory programs at such funding levels), as in effect on September 30, 2012, shall continue, and the Secretary of Agriculture shall carry out the authorities, until the later of—
qwen_chat.b:
Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section extends authorities for various programs (like conservation or research), it implicitly requires participation if those underlying programs involve public comment or advisory boards. However, this section itself is purely an extension of authority and funding authorization; it does not create new participation mechanisms, nor does it explicitly mandate consultation with outside parties in the text provided. It merely continues existing laws. The definition requires the section *itself* to involve participation. Since this section is a "continuing resolution" style extension, it does not contain the procedural language of participation (e.g., "shall consult," "public hearing," "advisory committee").

Another tempting reading: The section mentions "Socially Disadvantaged Farmers or Ranchers" and "Outreach." One might think outreach implies participation. However, "outreach" is typically a one-way communication from the government to the public, not a two-way consultation or coordination required before a decision. The text here only authorizes funding for such programs, it does not describe the participatory process itself.

Therefore, the label is "No".
